notes.what: Campaign #446 W2-A: the CUDA profile that decides issue #446 scope item 1 (Axpy wire-or-delete) under a rule pre-registered BEFORE any number was measured. Four legs on ModernBERT-large: three SHIPPED dtype legs (L1 f32, L2 bf16, L3 f16, default admission) and one eager-AdamW CONTROL (L4 bf16, JAMMI_KERNELS_DISABLE=adamw_step_fused).
notes.method_lineage: Producer copies ci/scripts/perf/profile_356_legs.sh's run_traced / nsys-export / kernel_census.py invocation shape verbatim, including unit-356's declared-workload pins (--validation-fraction 0 --early-stopping-metric train_loss --epochs 1 --grad-accum 1, fixed --eval-cadence, --early-stopping-patience 10000) that make the non-training-step work identical across the (N, M) pair so it cancels in the differencing. Steps are rows/batch at --epochs 1; N=100, M=600, both multiples of 50.
notes.contract_document_absent: The task brief named `scratchpad/contract-356-profile.md` (Method / Census / Wall denominator sections) as a READ-FIRST input. That file does not exist anywhere on this machine or in the repository (searched /private/tmp/claude-501/** and `git ls-files`); only its CONSUMERS survive. The pins above were therefore taken from the tracked consumers that quote it verbatim -- profile_356_legs.sh's own header (## Declared workload, WALL DENOMINATOR v4, STEP-COUNT PIN v4) and kernel_census.py's module doc -- never reconstructed from memory.
recorded_deviations: BATCH: the leg table declared b=8; ModernBERT-large at b=8/W=512 OOMs on this A100 80GB in EVERY leg configuration (DriverError(CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY) out of `Encoder forward: LoRA`, sampled device high-water mark 75757 MiB of 81920 MiB, GPU otherwise idle at 0 MiB used with no other compute apps). A live capacity probe cleared b=4 for all four configurations (f32/f16/bf16 fused and the eager-AdamW control) and b=2 as well; b=4 was taken as the largest that fits and is SHARED by every leg, since a per-leg batch would make the per-step denominators -- and therefore P -- incomparable. P is a RATIO of per-step GPU time, so it remains exactly the pre-registered quantity; only the absolute per-step times move. 4 also still divides the held-out fixture's 128 pairs, which finetune_run refuses otherwise.

gen_fixed_width_corpus.py --verify-tokenizer IS supported and WAS attempted on every leg; it REFUSES against ModernBERT's tokenizer.json with `'approach' -> 2 wordpieces (expected 1)`. That flag asserts every _VOCAB word is a single WordPiece, an assumption written for BERT-style WordPiece tokenizers; ModernBERT ships BPE. The direction is harmless to the pin the corpus exists to satisfy (every text > --max-seq-length, so truncation makes every row exactly W wide) because a multi-token vocab word only ever INCREASES a text's token count. The pin was therefore MEASURED directly instead of inherited: every leg encodes a deterministic stride sample of its own generated corpus with this checkpoint's own tokenizer and records the min/max, and a leg whose measured minimum is not > W is INVALID. Measured min was 515 tokens against W=512 on every leg.

The per-leg .nsys-rep / .sqlite captures and the generated corpora were deleted on-pod after BOTH consumers (kernel_census.py, axpy_pair_census.py) had read them -- a 600-step W=512 trace is multi-GB twice over and four legs would exhaust the pod mid-sweep. census.json / axpy_pairs.json / manifest.json are the records (the same deviation unit-356's own close-out artifact recorded), and each corpus's sha256 is kept so the byte-for-byte regenerability of `--seed 42` stays checkable rather than asserted.

decision_rule.written_before_measurement: The rule below was written in scratchpad/w2-axpy-preregistration.md BEFORE any leg ran on this pod -- it fixes the threshold (2.0%), the second limb (one dispatch site >= 50% of P), the definition of P, and the explicit statement that the eager-AdamW control leg cannot by itself justify wiring. It is reproduced here verbatim so the artifact carries the rule it was judged under, not a rule reconstructed after the numbers were seen.
decision_rule.text: WIRE axpy iff P >= 2.0% of per-step GPU time on ANY shipped leg (L1/L2/L3) AND a single dispatch site in the training graph covers >= 50% of P (so one admit() site captures a real, attributable win — a fused op with no dominant call site is manifest noise). Otherwise DELETE in full. The eager-AdamW control leg (L4) cannot by itself justify wiring: it is a fallback the shipped path does not take, so a large P on L4 alone is recorded as an honest negative for axpy and as a data point for fused-AdamW coverage, never as a wire decision.
decision_rule.P_definition: P = (per-step GPU time of axpy-SHAPED PAIRS) / gpu_kernel_us_per_step, both differenced over the same (N=100, M=600) same-workload pair. An axpy-shaped PAIR is an `affine_*` launch whose output feeds a `badd_*`/`bsub_*` on identically-shaped operands. Confirmed from the nsys sqlite's own KERNEL START ORDERING, not by launch-count matching alone: the add must be the affine's IMMEDIATE SUCCESSOR within the same (device, context, stream) -- where kernels are serialized, so the immediate successor is the launch that consumed its output if anything did -- must carry an IDENTICAL (gridX,Y,Z, blockX,Y,Z) signature (an elementwise launch's grid is a function of its element count, so an equal signature is the census-visible witness of identically-shaped operands), and must share the affine's dtype suffix (Axpy is same-dtype by domain, ops/axpy.rs). BOTH launches' time is counted, because one Axpy launch is exactly what replaces both (ops/axpy.rs: 'It fuses exactly one affine(alpha) + one badd -- two launches and one extra memory pass -- into one launch').
decision_rule.threshold_rationale: From the pre-registration, verbatim: the campaign #356 fusion levers were sized against a 191 ms / 673 ms (28%) gap and each landed lever removed >= 19 ms (>= 2.8%); a fused op below 2% of step time cannot be measured against the aa-null band (ci/scripts/check_aa_null_band.py) with the 3-seed protocol the perf gate uses, so it could never carry a perf claim -- and an op that cannot carry a claim has no honest home in the release manifest.

verdict.reasoning: limb A (max P over valid shipped legs >= 0.02): max P = 0.0269% on L3 -> FAILS; limb B (one dispatch site covers >= 0.5 of P on L3): strict (admit()-able) top site covers 0.0% of P -> FAILS; lenient (any source location) top site covers 100.0% -> HOLDS. Conjunction -> DELETE (identical under either limb-B reading, since limb A fails on its own).

limb_a_P_threshold.test: max P over valid shipped legs >= 0.02

limb_b_single_site.test: one dispatch site covers >= 0.5 of P on L3

sites.name: candle autograd — Op::Affine gradient accumulation
sites.code: Op::Affine { arg, mul, .. } => { let arg_grad = grad.affine(*mul, 0.)?; let sum_grad = grads.or_insert(arg)?; *sum_grad = sum_grad.add(&arg_grad)? }
sites.why_this_is_the_generator: `grad.affine(mul, 0.)` emits one affine_<dtype> launch and `sum_grad.add(&arg_grad)` emits one badd_<dtype> launch on an identically-shaped operand, back to back on the same stream — literally `y + alpha*x`, i.e. an exact Axpy(alpha=mul). The arm runs once per Op::Affine NODE in the backward walk, so it is a generic autograd accumulation rather than one call site with one shape.
sites.why_not_admittable: It is inside candle-core's own backward() loop. jammi does not dispatch through it and cannot place an admission::admit() there without patching upstream, which the house doctrine forbids (extend seams, not upstream). Under the rule's own parenthetical ('one admit() site captures a real, attributable win') this contributes 0% admit()-able coverage of P.
which_forward_affines_feed_it: trainer.rs mnrl_loss: `sim = contiguous_matmul(a_norm, p_t) * scale` and `(row_loss + col_loss) * 0.5` — (n,n) and scalar tensors (the grid[1,1,1] bucket)
trainer.rs l2_normalize_rows: the sqr/sum_keepdim/sqrt/clamp/broadcast_div chain — the eq_f32 / cast_u8_f32 neighbours in the signatures are its clamp backward
candle_nn::loss::cross_entropy's log_softmax + nll — the uexp / ulog / gather_u32 / sa_u32 (scatter-add) neighbours in the signatures
the pooled-embedding path: batch x hidden = 4 x 1024 (grid[4]) and the jointly-encoded anchor+positive 2 x batch x hidden = 8 x 1024 (grid[8])
sites.signature_evidence: On every leg the dominant neighbourhood is `uexp/ulog/gather_u32/fast_sum/sa_u32/eq/cast_u8` around the pair — a cross-entropy and normalisation backward, NOT a transformer block (which would show ampere_*gemm / layer_norm / flash_* / rope neighbours).

limb_b_single_site.note: both readings are reported because they DIFFER on this measurement; the rule is a conjunction and limb A fails, so the verdict is the same either way and no reading had to be chosen to reach it

control_leg_record.P_vs_threshold: BELOW the 2.0% threshold even on its own terms
control_leg_record.why_it_cannot_wire: Pre-registered before measurement: this is the F32-only FALLBACK arm the shipped path does not take. Every shipped leg measured adamw_eager_dispatches == 0 and adamw_fused_dispatches == 224/step — the fused adamw_step_fused_t kernel admitted on every trainable Var, every step, on all three dtypes. So the axpy-shaped work this leg exposes is work the shipped binary never does.
control_leg_record.what_it_IS_a_data_point_for: fused-AdamW coverage, exactly as the pre-registration says. Forcing the eager arm adds 15 launches per Var per step in place of 3 and costs 0.0533 s/step of wall (22.7% over the identical fused leg L2), of which the axpy-shaped pairs are 0.003038 s/step. The fused kernel is what keeps this off the shipped path; Axpy is not needed to keep it off.
control_leg_record.honest_negative_for_axpy: The one place in jammi's own code where axpy-shaped pairs are both dominant and admit()-able is a fallback that never runs in the shipped configuration. That is a negative result for Axpy, recorded as such.

measurement_method.producer: ci/scripts/perf/profile_446_axpy_legs.sh (this artifact's producer), which drives ci/scripts/perf/gen_fixed_width_corpus.py, nsys profile --trace=cuda, nsys export --type=sqlite, ci/scripts/perf/kernel_census.py, and ci/scripts/perf/axpy_pair_census.py.
measurement_method.differencing: Each leg is TWO traced runs of the SAME declared workload at N=100 and M=600 optimizer steps (steps = rows/batch at --epochs 1; the N corpus is a literal line-PREFIX of the M corpus, so the two runs train identical rows in identical order for their shared first N steps). Every reported per-step quantity is (M-run minus N-run) / (M-N). Model load, the init probe, the held-out eval and checkpointing are identical across the pinned pair and cancel exactly.
measurement_method.wall_denominator: wall_s_per_step = (train_run_wall_s_M - train_run_wall_s_N) / (M-N), each read from tiers.finetune_run of that run's own report JSON and passed to kernel_census.py as --wall-a/--wall-b -- the same (M-N)-step differencing applied to the wall clock.
measurement_method.validity_refusals: kernel_census.py refuses (leg INVALID, no report) on a missing or present-but-empty CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_KERNEL table, on steps_b <= steps_a, on any negative per-key count delta beyond tolerance, on a positive-count bucket with a negative time delta, on a fixed-cost bucket whose time jitter exceeds its hybrid floor/relative bound, and on an empty differenced census. axpy_pair_census.py refuses on the same two instrument failures, on a negative differenced pair time, on a negative differenced AdamW dispatch delta, and on ANY non-finite headline -- explicitly, because `nan >= 0.02` is False and an unguarded threshold check would silently read a diverged run as a clean below-threshold DELETE.
measurement_method.adamw_sanity_check: Each leg's declared arm is confirmed against the trace, with the trainable-Var count V MEASURED rather than assumed: V = (adamw_dispatches_M - adamw_dispatches_N) / (M-N) from the runs' own report counters. AdamW::step's fused arm is ONE adamw_step_fused_t call per Var = THREE launches (two InplaceOp2 moment updates -> adamw_moment_update_f32, one InplaceOp3 theta update -> adamw_theta_update_f32); the eager arm is step_eager_one's candle chain (affine x8, badd x2, bsub, bdiv, usqr, usqrt) plus three Var::set copies. SHIPPED legs must show adamw_moment_update_f32 ~ 2V/step and adamw_theta_update_f32 ~ 1V/step with zero eager dispatches; the CONTROL leg must show BOTH fused kernels ABSENT, zero fused dispatches, V eager dispatches per step, and every eager-chain family present. A leg failing this is INVALID and contributes no P to the verdict.

cross_leg_eager_chain_oracle.what: L4 minus L2 per-step launch counts must equal step_eager_one's own per-Var chain multiplicities times the MEASURED trainable-Var count. L4 and L2 differ in exactly one thing (the optimizer arm), so this is an independent second route to 'the control leg really ran the arm it claims' — the counters and the trace are separate instruments.

whole_trace_launch_identity.statement: launches_per_step(L4) == launches_per_step(L2) + 15*V (eager chain added) - 3*V (fused launches removed)
whole_trace_launch_identity.note: the per-family deltas also sum to the same eager-chain total (3360.0 == 3360.0), so the family table and the whole-trace identity are consistent with each other as well

instrument_validation.what: axpy_pair_census.py is a NEW measuring instrument, so its own answer was checked against a hand-constructed oracle before it was pointed at any real trace -- a number is measured-and-asserted, never transcribed.
instrument_validation.oracle: Two synthetic nsys-shaped sqlite exports whose axpy-pair answer is known in closed form by construction: each synthetic step unit emits exactly 2 true pairs worth 800 ns, alongside four DECOYS that must NOT be counted (an affine->badd with a mismatched grid; an affine whose successor is a matmul; an affine_bf16 followed by a badd_f32; an affine and an add on DIFFERENT streams), a fixed-cost affine->badd prefix present identically in both exports (which must CANCEL, not inflate P), and 2 x adamw_moment_update_f32 + 1 x adamw_theta_update_f32 per step.
instrument_validation.asserted: axpy_pair_us_per_step == 0.8, P == 0.0008, pairs_per_step == 2.0, pair buckets == 2, moment launches/step == 2.0, theta launches/step == 1.0, trainable Vars/step == 1.0, sanity ok, exit 0 -- all PASS.
refusals_driven_non_vacuously: a trace whose fused-kernel launch counts do not match 2V/1V (exit 4) -- this case caught a real error in the oracle's OWN first draft, which declared 12 Vars against a 1-Var trace, so the multiplier check is demonstrably not vacuous
a NON-FINITE denominator (exit 3) -- the negative control that matters, since `nan >= 0.02` is False and a naive threshold check would pass silently on a diverged path
a fused-declared leg whose counters show it dispatched eager (exit 4)
an eager-control leg still launching the fused kernels (exit 4)

sites.name: candle autograd — Op::Affine gradient accumulation
sites.code: Op::Affine { arg, mul, .. } => { let arg_grad = grad.affine(*mul, 0.)?; let sum_grad = grads.or_insert(arg)?; *sum_grad = sum_grad.add(&arg_grad)? }
sites.why_this_is_the_generator: `grad.affine(mul, 0.)` emits one affine_<dtype> launch and `sum_grad.add(&arg_grad)` emits one badd_<dtype> launch on an identically-shaped operand, back to back on the same stream — literally `y + alpha*x`, i.e. an exact Axpy(alpha=mul). The arm runs once per Op::Affine NODE in the backward walk, so it is a generic autograd accumulation rather than one call site with one shape.
sites.why_not_admittable: It is inside candle-core's own backward() loop. jammi does not dispatch through it and cannot place an admission::admit() there without patching upstream, which the house doctrine forbids (extend seams, not upstream). Under the rule's own parenthetical ('one admit() site captures a real, attributable win') this contributes 0% admit()-able coverage of P.

sites.name: jammi AdamW eager fallback arm — step_eager_one
sites.code: let next_m = ((m*beta1)? + (g*(1.0-beta1))?)?;  let next_v = ((v*beta2)? + (g.sqr()?*(1.0-beta2))?)?;  ...  let next_theta = (next_theta - (adjusted_grad*lr)?)?;
sites.why_this_is_the_generator: Three of this chain's fifteen launches per Var are axpy-shaped by construction: the two tensor `+`s (each preceded by an affine — `m*beta1 + g*(1-beta1)` and `v*beta2 + g.sqr()*(1-beta2)`) and the one tensor `-` (`next_theta - adjusted_grad*lr`). The measurement closes on exactly that: 448 affine->badd pairs/step == 2 x V and 224 affine->bsub pairs/step == 1 x V, at the MEASURED V = 224 trainable Vars/step.
sites.why_it_still_cannot_carry_the_decision: PRE-REGISTERED, before any number existed: this is the F32-only FALLBACK arm the shipped path does not take. All three shipped legs measured adamw_eager_dispatches == 0 and adamw_fused_dispatches == 224/step, i.e. the fused adamw_step_fused_t kernel admitted on every Var, every step. The rule states that a large P on the control leg alone is 'recorded as an honest negative for axpy and as a data point for the fused-AdamW coverage, not as a wire decision'. And on its own terms it would fail anyway: P = 1.65% on L4 is still below the 2.0% threshold.
sites.var_shape_closure: The per-shape Var counts recovered from the 1-pair-per-Var affine->bsub buckets are {8192: 140, 41984: 28, 24576: 28, 21504: 28}, summing to 224 == the measured V. They reconstruct the LoRA parameter set exactly for ModernBERT-large (hidden 1024, intermediate 2624, 28 layers, rank 8) under the `Wqkv,Wo,Wi` selectors, where `Wo` matches BOTH attn.Wo and mlp.Wo: per layer, five 8x1024-element Vars (Wqkv.A, attn.Wo.A, attn.Wo.B, Wi.A, mlp.Wo.B), one 8x3072 (Wqkv.B), one 8x5248 (Wi.B — 2 x intermediate for GeGLU), one 8x2624 (mlp.Wo.A, launched on 21 blocks of 1024 = 21504 slots for 20992 elements). 8 Vars/layer x 28 layers = 224.
